speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the timeline and severity of your symptoms. Did your fever and flank pain start immediately after your sinusitis treatment, or did they develop a few days later? Additionally, how would you describe the nature of the pain in your side?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the antibiotic course you took include any penicillin or cephalosporin, and have you noticed any visible changes in your urine, such as cloudiness, blood, or a foul smell? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, CBC.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in your urine despite a negative bacterial culture is highly suggestive of an allergic interstitial nephritis, likely triggered by the penicillin or cephalosporin you took for your sinusitis. Do you recall any rash, hives, or itching that appeared while you were on the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to antibiotic exposure (likely cross-reactivity or re-challenge).

REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound to rule out hydronephrosis and assess kidney size.
